summary: This note outlines how education in the Philippines is governed by three bodies: the Department of Education (DepEd) for K-12 basic education, and the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) for higher and technical-vocational education. It also describes the start of the K-12 program, which was phased in beginning in school year 2011-2012 alongside a new nationwide curriculum.
one_line: Overview of the Philippine bodies that govern education (DepEd, CHED, TESDA) and the phased rollout of the K-12 system from 2011.
key_facts: Education in the Philippines is managed and regulated by the Department of Education (DepEd), Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA).
DepEd is responsible for the K-12 basic education system.
DepEd exercises full and exclusive control over public schools and nominal regulation over private schools.
DepEd enforces the national curriculum that has been put in place since 2013.
CHED is responsible for higher education and regulates the academically-oriented universities and colleges.
TESDA oversees the development of technical and vocational education institutions and programs in the country.
In 2011, the Department of Education started to implement the new K-12 educational system.
The new K-12 educational system included a new curriculum for all schools nationwide.
The K-12 program has a so-called phased implementation.
The phased implementation of the K-12 program started in school year 2011-2012.
